the transfer of nonesterified fatty acid analogs from phospholipids and lipoproteins to proteins is a first-order process and that the rate of transfer is a function of the acyl chain composition of the nonesterified fatty acyl chain.

the kinetics of NEFA transfer between lipid and protein membranes are slow relative to their rates of release from lipolytic processes and that they are dependent on the acy1 chain structure of the NEFA.

the kinetics of transfer of nonesterified fatty acid (NEFA) analogues from phospholipids, low density lipoproteids, high density lipoprotein, and proteins are first-order and characterized with similar rate constants.

the study of lipid-protein interactions.
understanding how the lipid and protein components of membranes and lipoproteins interact to form functional entities and how they respond to environmental changes.
the kinetics and mechanisms by which amphiphilic molecules spontaneously transfer between membranes and proteins.

the kinetics of NEFA transfer between phospholipid, lipoprotein, and protein surfaces is first-order and is characterized by similar rates.

the transfer of NEFA from lipids and lipoproteins to proteins is slow, and that the rate of transfer is determined by the structure of the NEFA and by the structure of both the lipid and protein surfaces.
the transfer of NEFA and lysophospholipids between lipid and protein surface is spontaneous and occurs with similar rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transfer of NEFA and other monoacyl amphipathic molecules between phospholipid membranes and proteins is a slow process that is dependent on the acylation of the amphipathic molecule, the structure of the acceptor, and the structure of the donor.
the transfer of NEFA from phospholipids and protein surfaces is a slow first-order process, and the rate is determined mainly by the structure of the acyl chain.
NEFA and lysolecethins are not simply released from membranes and lipoproteins but are transferred to the surface of the acceptor molecule.

the kinetics of transfer of NEFA and lysophospholipids from phospholipids and proteins are slow relative to lipolytic processes.
